_comment: Flashcards de la Parte 1 del NIE (1.3 y 1.2). Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

cards.front: Three parts of the actus reus?
cards.back: Conduct, circumstances and consequences (result).
Conduct crime: the act is enough (e.g. perjury). Result crime: a consequence must be caused (e.g. murder).
cards.es: Mera conducta vs. delito de resultado.

cards.back: No general duty to act – unless a recognised duty exists.
cards.es: No hay deber general de actuar.

cards.front: Six sources of a duty to act (+ case)?
cards.back: Statute · Contract (Pittwood) · Relationship (Gibbins & Proctor) · Assumed care (Stone & Dobinson; Instan) · Creating danger (Miller; Evans) · Public office (Dytham).
cards.es: Ley, contrato, relación, asumir cuidado, crear peligro, cargo público.

cards.back: Created a dangerous situation (cigarette fire), became aware and did nothing → duty to act.
cards.es: Creó el peligro y no hizo nada.

cards.back: Police officer watched a man being beaten to death → misconduct in public office.
'But for' test – R v White (1910).
Operating and substantial cause = more than minimal; need not be the only or main cause (Smith; Pagett).
cards.es: Causa operativa y sustancial, más que mínima.

cards.front: When does medical treatment break the chain?
cards.back: Only if so independent and potent that the wound is merely the setting (Cheshire). Jordan = wound nearly healed, palpably wrong (rare).
Take your victim as you find them, including beliefs – R v Blaue (1975).
cards.es: La víctima se toma como es.

cards.back: Free, deliberate, informed self-injection by an adult breaks the chain → supplier not guilty of manslaughter.
cards.es: La autoinyección libre rompe la cadena.

cards.back: Victim's escape breaks the chain only if 'daft' / unforeseeable.
cards.es: La huida solo rompe la cadena si es absurda.

cards.back: Human shield; police returned fire → defendant still the cause.
cards.es: Escudo humano: sigue siendo la causa.

cards.back: State of affairs offence: 'found drunk on a highway' after police put him there.
Aid, abet, counsel or procure – Accessories and Abettors Act 1861, s. 8 (tried and punished as principal).
Accessory must intend to assist or encourage; foresight is only evidence of intention.
cards.es: Hace falta intención; la previsión es solo indicio.

cards.back: The result is the defendant's aim or purpose (however unlikely).
Result a virtual certainty + defendant appreciated it → jury MAY find intention.
cards.es: Prácticamente seguro + se daba cuenta → el jurado PUEDE apreciar intención.

cards.back: Jury not bound to infer intention from natural and probable consequences; look at all the evidence.
Aware of a risk + unreasonable to take it in the circumstances known to them (subjective).
Intention or subjective recklessness.

cards.front: s. 20 OAPA – what must be foreseen?
cards.back: Some harm, not serious harm (Savage; Parmenter).
Deliberately or recklessly.
1) Defendant's actual knowledge/belief of facts; 2) dishonest by standards of ordinary decent people?
No mens rea needed for at least one element; presumption of mens rea (Sweet v Parsley; B v DPP).
Latimer: transfers to another victim. Pembliton: does not transfer to a different type of offence.
cards.es: Se transfiere solo al mismo tipo de delito.

cards.back: Continuing act: car on officer's foot; mens rea formed during the act → battery.
Series of acts treated as one transaction; mens rea at the start is enough.
Specific (murder, s. 18, theft): intoxication may negate intent. Basic (s. 20, s. 47, assault): voluntary intoxication no defence.
Objective: below the standard of a reasonable person.
